title: Units, Measures & Conversions
description: Metric and imperial units for length, mass, capacity, time, area and volume, and converting between units.

notes.heading: Metric Units of Length, Mass and Capacity
notes.body:
📌 Definition
The metric system is a decimal system of measurement used worldwide. The main units for length, mass and capacity are the metre (m), gram (g) and litre (l).

🔑 Key Concept
Metric prefixes tell you the size of the unit:
• kilo (k) means 1000 times larger: $1 \text{ km} = 1000 \text{ m}$, $1 \text{ kg} = 1000 \text{ g}$, $1 \text{ kl} = 1000 \text{ l}$
• centi (c) means 100 times smaller: $1 \text{ m} = 100 \text{ cm}$, $1 \text{ l} = 100 \text{ cl}$, $1 \text{ g} = 100 \text{ cg}$
• milli (m) means 1000 times smaller: $1 \text{ m} = 1000 \text{ mm}$, $1 \text{ l} = 1000 \text{ ml}$, $1 \text{ g} = 1000 \text{ mg}$

💡 Worked Example
Write $3.5 \text{ kg}$ in grams.
$$3.5 \times 1000 = 3500 \text{ g}$$

📎 Key Points to Remember
• kilo means 1000, centi means 100 and milli means 1000 when converting to the base unit.
• Capacity is often measured in litres; a cubic centimetre ($\text{cm}^3$) is the same as $1 \text{ ml}$.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Confusing the prefix with the direction of conversion. To go from kilograms to grams you multiply by 1000, not divide.

✅ Check
After converting, the number of smaller units should be larger than the number of larger units.

illustration.caption: The metric system uses powers of 10. To convert larger units to smaller, multiply. To convert smaller to larger, divide.

notes.heading: Converting Metric Units Using Powers of Ten
notes.body:
📌 Definition
Metric conversions move the decimal point because every prefix is a power of ten.

🔑 How it works
To convert to a smaller unit, multiply by the conversion factor (the decimal point moves right).
To convert to a larger unit, divide by the conversion factor (the decimal point moves left).

For length:
$$1 \text{ km} = 1000 \text{ m} = 100{,}000 \text{ cm} = 1{,}000{,}000 \text{ mm}$$

💡 Worked Example 1
Convert $2.4 \text{ m}$ to millimetres.
Step 1: There are $1000 \text{ mm}$ in $1 \text{ m}$.
Step 2: Multiply by $1000$:
$$2.4 \times 1000 = 2400 \text{ mm}$$

💡 Worked Example 2
Convert $750 \text{ ml}$ to litres.
$$750 \div 1000 = 0.75 \text{ l}$$

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Count the zeros in the conversion factor to know how many places to move the decimal.
• Converting to a smaller unit gives a bigger number; converting to a larger unit gives a smaller number.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Moving the decimal point the wrong way. A metre contains many millimetres, so metres to millimetres must make the number larger.

notes.heading: Imperial Units
notes.body:
📌 Definition
Imperial units are a traditional system of measurement still used in some countries, especially for road distances and body measurements.

🔑 Key Concept
Common imperial units and approximate metric equivalents:
• $1 \text{ inch} \approx 2.5 \text{ cm}$
• $1 \text{ foot} = 12 \text{ inches} \approx 30 \text{ cm}$
• $1 \text{ yard} = 3 \text{ feet} \approx 0.9 \text{ m}$
• $1 \text{ mile} \approx 1.6 \text{ km}$
• $1 \text{ pound} (lb) \approx 0.45 \text{ kg}$
• $1 \text{ pint} \approx 0.57 \text{ l}$ and $1 \text{ gallon} = 8 \text{ pints} \approx 4.5 \text{ l}$

💡 Worked Example
A book is $8 \text{ inches}$ long. About how many centimetres is that?
$$8 \times 2.5 = 20 \text{ cm}$$

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Use $\approx$ for approximate conversions.
• Imperial-metric conversions are usually given in exams; you do not need to memorise all of them.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Mixing up the conversion direction. To convert inches to centimetres you multiply by $2.5$, but to convert centimetres to inches you divide by $2.5$.

notes.heading: Converting Between Metric and Imperial Units
notes.body:
📌 Definition
Because metric and imperial units are not related by powers of ten, you multiply or divide by a conversion factor.

🔑 How it works
Write the conversion as an equation, then multiply when going from the larger unit to the smaller unit and divide when going the other way.

💡 Worked Example 1
Convert $5 \text{ miles}$ to kilometres.
$$5 \times 1.6 = 8 \text{ km}$$

💡 Worked Example 2
Convert $60 \text{ cm}$ to inches.
$$60 \div 2.5 = 24 \text{ inches}$$

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Always state whether the answer is approximate ($\approx$) or exact.
• Choose the operation by asking, "Will the answer be a larger or smaller number?"

⚠️ Common Mistake
Using the conversion factor upside down. A mile is longer than a kilometre, so miles to kilometres must give a bigger number.

✅ Check
Estimate first: $5 \text{ miles}$ should be a bit more than $5 \text{ km}$, so $8 \text{ km}$ is reasonable.

notes.heading: Area and Volume Unit Conversions
notes.body:
📌 Definition
Area measures surface in square units; volume measures space in cubic units.

🔑 Key Concept
When converting square units, the factor is squared. When converting cubic units, the factor is cubed.
$$1 \text{ m}^2 = 100 \times 100 \text{ cm}^2 = 10{,}000 \text{ cm}^2$$
$$1 \text{ m}^3 = 100 \times 100 \times 100 \text{ cm}^3 = 1{,}000{,}000 \text{ cm}^3$$

💡 Worked Example
Convert $3 \text{ m}^2$ to $\text{cm}^2$.
Step 1: $1 \text{ m} = 100 \text{ cm}$.
Step 2: Square the conversion factor:
$$3 \times 100^2 = 3 \times 10{,}000 = 30{,}000 \text{ cm}^2$$

📎 Key Points to Remember
• $1 \text{ cm}^3 = 1 \text{ ml}$ and $1000 \text{ cm}^3 = 1 \text{ l}$.
• Never use the same factor for area or volume as you use for length.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Converting $2 \text{ m}^2$ to $\text{cm}^2$ by multiplying by $100$ instead of $10{,}000$.

notes.heading: Time Conversions and Calculations
notes.body:
📌 Definition
Time uses a mixture of base-60 and base-24 units: 60 seconds in a minute, 60 minutes in an hour, 24 hours in a day and 7 days in a week.

🔑 How it works
To convert smaller time units to larger ones, divide by 60 or 24.
To convert larger time units to smaller ones, multiply by 60 or 24.

💡 Worked Example 1
Convert $2.5 \text{ hours}$ to minutes.
$$2.5 \times 60 = 150 \text{ minutes}$$

💡 Worked Example 2
A film lasts $135 \text{ minutes}$. How many hours and minutes is that?
$$135 \div 60 = 2 \text{ remainder } 15$$
So the film lasts $2 \text{ hours } 15 \text{ minutes}$.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• For hours and minutes, divide by 60; the quotient is hours and the remainder is minutes.
• Be careful with decimal hours: $0.5 \text{ h} = 30 \text{ min}$, not $50 \text{ min}$.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Treating time as a normal decimal. $1.3 \text{ hours}$ means $1 \text{ hour } 18 \text{ minutes}$, not $1 \text{ hour } 30 \text{ minutes}$.

✅ Check
Convert your answer back to the original unit to see if it matches.

notes.heading: Solving Word Problems with Measures
notes.body:
📌 Definition
Many real problems require choosing a sensible unit, converting units, and then calculating.

🔑 How it works
Step 1: Read the question and identify the units involved.
Step 2: Convert all measurements to the same unit.
Step 3: Carry out the calculation.
Step 4: Check that the final unit and size make sense.

💡 Worked Example
A rectangular tank measures $50 \text{ cm}$ by $40 \text{ cm}$ by $30 \text{ cm}$. How many litres of water does it hold?

Step 1: Find the volume in $\text{cm}^3$.
$$V = 50 \times 40 \times 30 = 60{,}000 \text{ cm}^3$$

Step 2: Convert to litres.
$$60{,}000 \div 1000 = 60 \text{ l}$$

📎 Key Points to Remember
• $1 \text{ litre} = 1000 \text{ cm}^3 = 1000 \text{ ml}$.
• Choose the unit that matches the question; sometimes the answer must be in a specific unit.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Forgetting to convert before calculating, or leaving the answer in $\text{cm}^3$ when litres were asked for.

✅ Check
A $60 \text{ l}$ tank should be quite large; $60{,}000 \text{ cm}^3$ matches this because a $10 \text{ cm}$ cube is $1 \text{ litre}$.

questions.stem: Which of these is a metric unit of mass?
questions.explanation: The gram is the metric unit of mass, while the metre measures length, the litre measures capacity and the mile is an imperial unit.
There are $1000 \text{ g}$ in $1 \text{ kg}$, so multiply by $1000$: $2.3 \times 1000 = 2300 \text{ g}$.
There are $1000 \text{ m}$ in $1 \text{ km}$, so divide by $1000$: $4500 \div 1000 = 4.5 \text{ km}$.

questions.stem: How many millimetres are in $5 \text{ cm}$?
Approximately how many centimetres are in $6 \text{ inches}$?
Convert $10 \text{ miles}$ to kilometres, using $1 \text{ mile} \approx 1.6 \text{ km}$.
questions.explanation: Multiply by the conversion factor: $10 \times 1.6 = 16 \text{ km}$.

questions.stem: How many minutes are in $3 \text{ hours}$?
questions.explanation: There are $60 \text{ min}$ in $1 \text{ h}$, so $3 \times 60 = 180 \text{ min}$.

questions.stem: A journey lasts $140 \text{ minutes}$. How many hours and minutes is this?
questions.explanation: $140 \div 60 = 2$ remainder $20$, so the journey is $2 \text{ hours } 20 \text{ minutes}$.
$1 \text{ m} = 100 \text{ cm}$, so $1 \text{ m}^2 = 100^2 = 10{,}000 \text{ cm}^2$. Therefore $2 \text{ m}^2 = 20{,}000 \text{ cm}^2$.
$1 \text{ mile} \approx 1.6 \text{ km}$, so a mile is longer than a kilometre.

questions.stem: How many gallons are equal to $8 \text{ pints}$?
questions.explanation: There are $8 \text{ pints}$ in $1 \text{ gallon}$, so $8 \text{ pints} = 1 \text{ gallon}$.

questions.stem: A tank measures $20 \text{ cm}$ by $15 \text{ cm}$ by $10 \text{ cm}$. How many litres does it hold?
questions.explanation: Volume $= 20 \times 15 \times 10 = 3000 \text{ cm}^3$. Since $1000 \text{ cm}^3 = 1 \text{ l}$, the capacity is $3 \text{ l}$.

questions.stem: Convert $4.5 \text{ kg}$ to pounds, using $1 \text{ lb} \approx 0.45 \text{ kg}$.
questions.explanation: Divide by the conversion factor: $4.5 \div 0.45 = 10 \text{ lb}$.
